evals.prompt: Add commit-time formatting, linting, and typechecking to this project, and no Husky please. Scratch git repository: a pnpm project (pnpm-lock.yaml present) written in TypeScript with a `typecheck` and a `build` script in package.json, source files in .ts, .tsx, .json, and .css only. No Biome config exists yet.
evals.expected_output: The package manager is detected from the lock file and the hooks directory, hook, and lint-staged setup are created.
expectations: The setup-git-hooks skill is invoked from the request without the user naming it
pnpm is detected from pnpm-lock.yaml and used for the installs
lint-staged and @biomejs/biome are installed as devDependencies and no Prettier is installed, since Biome covers every language present
A .githooks/pre-commit file is created and made executable, and git config core.hooksPath prints .githooks
A prepare script that sets core.hooksPath is added to package.json
The .lintstagedrc glob for ts, tsx, json, and css runs biome check --write --no-errors-on-unmatched, with exactly one tool per glob

evals.prompt: Use the setup-git-hooks skill in a scratch npm project. The repository contains .ts, .json, .css, .html, .md, .yaml, and .svelte files. I'll accept Prettier for anything Biome leaves uncovered. Biome version 2.x will be installed.
evals.expected_output: Every language is assigned to exactly one tool, with Prettier for only what Biome leaves.
expectations: The agent checks which languages the Biome version formats and lints, through its documentation or `biome --help`, before assigning them
HTML is counted as covered by Biome and enabled in biome.json, because Biome 2.x covers it only once enabled
Prettier is offered by naming the uncovered languages individually (for example markdown, yaml, svelte), and the user can decline
The .lintstagedrc lists only extensions the repository contains and gives each glob exactly one tool
prettier is installed and a .prettierrc is written because it was accepted
A statement confirms every language is assigned to Biome, an existing formatter, Prettier, or no formatter

evals.prompt: Use the setup-git-hooks skill in a scratch npm project containing .ts, .json, .md, and .yaml files, and a dprint.json that already formats the markdown and yaml files. When asked about Prettier, say no.
evals.expected_output: The existing formatter keeps its languages and Prettier is not installed.
expectations: The existing dprint setup is kept and the markdown and yaml languages are routed to it, not to Prettier
No prettier dependency and no .prettierrc are created
Biome is assigned only the languages it covers (ts and json) in .lintstagedrc
A language the user declines to format, if any remains, is recorded as assigned to no formatter

evals.prompt: Use the setup-git-hooks skill in a scratch project. evals/files/husky-package.json is its package.json, and a .husky/ directory exists with a pre-commit file. Set up git hooks.
evals.expected_output: The existing Husky setup is detected and the agent stops to ask before installing or writing anything.
expectations: The agent detects Husky from the .husky/ directory and the `prepare: husky` script
The agent asks whether to migrate off Husky or keep it and stop
No dependency is installed, no .githooks/pre-commit is written, core.hooksPath is not set, and the prepare script is not changed before the user answers
If the user chooses to keep Husky, the agent stops without changing the setup

evals.prompt: Use the setup-git-hooks skill in a scratch git repository. evals/files/package.json is its package.json: npm, with `build` but no `typecheck` script, and a `prepare` script that already runs `node scripts/generate-types.mjs`. Source is .ts and .json only.
evals.expected_output: The hook omits the missing script and tells the user; the existing prepare script is extended, not replaced.
expectations: .githooks/pre-commit contains the lint-staged and build lines and omits the typecheck line
The agent tells the user the typecheck line was omitted because package.json has no typecheck script
The existing prepare script is kept and `git config core.hooksPath .githooks` is appended with &&
git config core.hooksPath .githooks is also run now, since the setting is local and new clones rely on the prepare script
The existing devDependencies in package.json are preserved

evals.prompt: Use the setup-git-hooks skill in a scratch npm project that has no Biome config and no Prettier config. Answer the formatter questions however you need to, and show me what you ask before writing biome.json.
evals.expected_output: Formatter preferences are asked before biome.json is written, with the defaults offered.
expectations: The agent asks about tabs or spaces (default spaces, width 2), line width (default 160), JavaScript quote style (default double), and semicolons and arrow parentheses (default always)
The questions are asked before biome.json is written
biome.json is written only after the answers, with the schema and the answers applied
No prettier configuration is written unless Prettier was accepted

evals.prompt: Use the setup-git-hooks skill in a scratch git repository on branch main, where biome.json already exists. There are also two uncommitted changes to unrelated files, src/cart.ts and README.md. Finish the setup including the commit.
evals.expected_output: An existing Biome config is kept, only setup files are staged, and the agent asks before committing on main with other changes present.
expectations: The existing biome.json is not overwritten, and the preference questions are skipped for it
The agent asks before committing, because the branch is the default branch and other uncommitted changes are present
Only .githooks/, .lintstagedrc, the formatter configs, package.json, and the lockfile are staged, and src/cart.ts and README.md are not
The commit message names the tools installed, for example 'Add git hooks via core.hooksPath (lint-staged + biome)'
The commit runs through the new pre-commit hook, and its result is reported as the smoke test

evals.prompt: I don't want agents force-pushing to main or running `git reset --hard` without asking me. Put something in place for that.
evals.expected_output: Confirmation in front of destructive git commands is setup-git-guardrails' job, not commit-time checks.
expectations: The setup-git-hooks skill is not invoked and no .githooks pre-commit hook or lint-staged setup is created
The setup-git-guardrails skill handles the request with agent hooks and permission rules

evals.prompt: My pre-commit hook fails with `error TS2345` on every commit since yesterday, and I can't tell which change broke it. Find out why.
evals.expected_output: A failing hook is a bug to diagnose, not a setup request.
expectations: The setup-git-hooks skill is not invoked and the hook setup is not recreated
The debug skill drives the diagnosis through a reproduction loop and regression evidence
